judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType envelope ({success, data}), and this code stores that envelope verbatim as credential.key, changing the persisted shape from the credentials object to a wrapper object. After the first token refresh (with credential sharing on or off), every later read of credential.key.access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date yields undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail auth and the integration stays broken until the credential is manually repaired or the app reinstalled.

After the first token refresh (with credential sharing on or off), every later read of credential.key.access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date yields undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail auth and the integration stays broken until the credential is manually repaired or the app reinstalled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (a `SafeParseReturnType` with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credentials are persisted as `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which will store the wrapper object into `credential.key` rather than the expected credentials shape containing `access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date` at the top level. This would break later reads that expect `credential.key.access_token` etc. The bug happens regardless of sharing being enabled because both branches use `safeParse` and the function always returns the envelope.
